title: Cloud Infrastructure Trends 2026
description: Cloud Infrastructure Trends 2026: where cloud spending is growing, how enterprises are balancing multi-cloud and cost control, and what buyers should evaluate in infrastructure platforms.
keyFindings: The cloud infrastructure segment shows 23% year-over-year growth in 2026
Enterprise adoption of cloud infrastructure solutions increased by 40% compared to last year
62% of organizations report improved outcomes after implementing cloud infrastructure software
Small and medium businesses account for 56% of cloud infrastructure software spending
AI-powered features are the top consideration for 56% of buyers evaluating cloud infrastructure platforms
Cloud-based deployment represents 79% of new cloud infrastructure software installations
Integration capabilities influence 73% of purchasing decisions
cloud infrastructure software budgets increased by an average of 23% in 2026

sections.title: The State of Cloud Infrastructure
sections.body: Cloud infrastructure growth continues but is maturing: our data shows 23% year-over-year growth in 2026, down from the peak expansion years. Compute, storage, and networking are increasingly consumed through managed platforms rather than raw instances, and the conversation among buyers has shifted from whether to migrate to how to control the resulting spend.

sections.title: Enterprise Adoption
sections.body: Enterprise adoption of cloud infrastructure solutions increased 40% compared to last year. Large organizations are standardizing on a small set of cloud platforms, consolidating accounts, and centralizing identity and cost management. The reported driver is operational control, not just scalability.

sections.title: Spending and Cost Control
sections.body: Small and medium businesses account for 56% of cloud infrastructure spending, and budgets grew by an average of 23% in 2026. Cost management has become a first-class purchase: FinOps tools, rightsizing recommendations, and reserved capacity planning are increasingly part of the infrastructure stack rather than an afterthought.

sections.title: What Buyers Evaluate
sections.body: AI-powered features are the top consideration for 56% of buyers evaluating cloud infrastructure platforms, from managed GPU offerings to AI-assisted operations. Integration capabilities influence 73% of purchasing decisions, with buyers expecting the infrastructure layer to connect cleanly to their CI/CD, monitoring, and security tooling.

sections.title: Regional Deployment Patterns
sections.body: Cloud-based deployment represents 79% of new infrastructure installations, with providers expanding regional availability to serve data-residency and latency requirements. Multi-cloud remains common in enterprises, but our data shows most teams reducing the number of providers they actively operate rather than adding more.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.body: Standardize the account structure and identity model before adding workloads, and put cost visibility in place from the first month. Pilot any new infrastructure platform on a non-critical service, measure performance and spend against the current baseline, and review the portfolio quarterly. Treat FinOps as a permanent function rather than a one-time exercise.

methodology: This research is based on a survey of 2423 IT decision-makers, analysis of 82 software vendors, and secondary research from industry analysts. Data was collected in Q1-Q2 2026.
author: PilotStack Research Team
